findings.problem: fs::read_to_string(path).unwrap() panics on any I/O failure (missing file, permissions, disk full).
findings.failure_mode: Untrusted or transient I/O errors abort the process instead of returning a typed domain error.
findings.fix: Return Result<Vec<Record>, std::io::Error> and propagate with ? or map_err with a domain error type.

findings.problem: parts[1].parse::<u32>().unwrap() panics on non-numeric input in the value field.
findings.failure_mode: Malformed CSV rows cause a panic instead of returning a typed parse error.
findings.fix: Use .parse::<u32>().map_err(|e| ParseError::InvalidValue(e))? or equivalent with a domain error type, propagate up through Result.

findings.problem: parts[0] accesses the Vec by index without bounds check. If the line has no commas, this panics.
findings.failure_mode: Empty or whitespace-only lines cause a panic at runtime.

findings.problem: parts[1] accesses the Vec by index without bounds check. If the line has only one comma-separated field, this panics.
findings.failure_mode: Lines missing the value column panic at runtime.
findings.fix: Use parts.get(1).ok_or(ParseError::MissingField("value")) or restructure with split_once(',') for the two-field case.

findings.problem: as u16 on a u32 parse result is an unchecked width reduction. Values > 65535 silently overflow.
findings.failure_mode: Large numeric values wrap silently, producing incorrect records with no error signal.
findings.fix: Use u16::try_from(parsed_u32).map_err(ParseError::ValueOutOfRange) to reject values outside the u16 range.

findings.problem: println!("loaded {}", parts[0]) is a side effect embedded in data-loading logic. I/O side effects belong exclusively in the imperative shell.
findings.failure_mode: Hidden console I/O makes the function non-deterministic, non-testable, and couples data parsing to a concrete output target.
findings.fix: Remove println! entirely from the parsing function. If logging is needed, return a separate trace structure from the shell layer, not from the core parser.

findings.problem: split(',').map(|part| part.trim().to_string()).collect() allocates a full Vec<String> when only the first two fields are needed. SKILL.md mandates split_once for first-delimiter extraction.
findings.failure_mode: Unnecessary heap allocation per line; also forces parsing every field even when only the first two matter.
findings.fix: Use line.split_once(',').ok_or(ParseError::MissingField("delimiter")) to extract name and value parts, then trim and parse each independently.

findings.problem: value is a raw u16 with no domain constraint encoded in the type. A Record could hold any u16 including values outside valid domain bounds.
findings.failure_mode: Illegal domain values are representable at the type level; the compiler cannot enforce domain invariants.
findings.fix: Introduce a named newtype struct RecordValue(u16) with a fallible constructor that enforces domain bounds, and use RecordValue in Record.

findings.problem: load_samples returns Vec<Record> with no Result wrapper. All fallible I/O and parsing must return typed errors per Holzman Rust.
findings.failure_mode: Callers cannot distinguish between partial parse success and total failure; the function swallows errors via unwrap.
findings.fix: Change signature to pub fn load_samples(path: &str) -> Result<Vec<Record>, LoadError> where LoadError is a domain enum covering IoError, ParseError, and ValueOutOfRange.

findings.problem: collect() into Vec<String> has no bounded capacity and no allocation failure handling. SKILL.md requires try_reserve with checked_add/checked_mul for bounded capacity.
findings.failure_mode: A very large file can OOM or trigger OOM-killer; allocation failure is silently converted to continued execution with partial data.
findings.fix: Pre-allocate with a line-count estimate via try_reserve, compute capacity with checked_add/checked_mul, and handle AllocationError by returning a typed error.

missing_evidence: no benchmark exists for load_samples throughput or allocation behavior
no profiler data (perf/flamegraph) to validate allocation patterns
no allocation audit (e.g., dtree or heaptrack) for Vec<String> per-line allocations
no second-ring validation (e.g., proptest/fuzz) for malformed CSV input
no command-level evidence that cargo test or cargo clippy passes
no benchmark/profiler evidence to justify the current parsing approach for the expected input size
residual_risk: Static review only; no commands run. The crate has pervasive unwrap() usage, unchecked indexing, lossy casts, hidden I/O side effects, and missing error taxonomy. All are runtime panic or silent-misbehavior risks that require implementation repair and post-repair command evidence (cargo test, cargo clippy, cargo bench) to fully close.
